subject: Copywriting
title: The Four U's Formula
description: A 60-second lesson on The Four U's Formula.

hook.text: Great headlines share four traits: Useful, Urgent, Unique, and Ultra-specific. Miss one and the headline weakens.

buildup.text: Useful: it promises value. Urgent: it demands action now. Unique: it stands out. Ultra-specific: it's precise.

discovery.text: 'Lose 10 Pounds in 30 Days' hits all four. Useful, urgent, unique angle, specific numbers. That's why it works.

twist.text: Most headlines hit two U's at best. The gap between good and great is usually the missing third or fourth.

climax.text: The formula isn't a rule—it's a diagnostic tool. Score your headline on all four before publishing.

punchline.text: Four U's. Most headlines only hit two. Now you know why.

quiz.question: Which is NOT one of the Four U's of headline writing?

details.summary: The Four U's formula states that effective headlines should be Useful, Urgent, Unique, and Ultra-specific. Developed by copywriting coach Michael Masterson, this checklist gives writers a practical scoring system for evaluating headline strength before publishing.
details.whyItMatters: The Four U's provide an objective framework for headline evaluation. Instead of relying on instinct, writers can systematically improve headlines by scoring each element.
takeaways: Headlines should be Useful, Urgent, Unique, and Ultra-specific
Rate each U on a 1-4 scale to evaluate headline strength
A headline scoring high on all four U's is virtually guaranteed to perform

faq.question: How do you use the Four U's to score a headline?
faq.answer: Rate each U from 1 (weak) to 4 (strong). Useful: does it promise a benefit? Urgent: is there a reason to read now? Unique: is it unlike other headlines? Ultra-specific: does it include concrete details? A headline should score at least 3 on each dimension.

faq.question: Do all four U's need to be present in every headline?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Some headlines dominate on two or three U's and still work brilliantly. 'They Laughed When I Sat Down at the Piano' is unique and ultra-specific but not explicitly urgent. The framework is a diagnostic tool, not a rigid formula.
